question: How does BSP actually buy companies?
html:
BSP buys theme-first, in banked processes, with two seller types: sponsor secondaries for larger checks and founder or partner owners for smaller ones. These patterns come from public evidence, not BSP's internal screening criteria (BSP acquisition methodology).

Thesis comes before the deal

  • Each deal is presented as the result of sector work done in advance. RJ David spent "over a year" in electrical services before CET (BSP acquisition methodology).
  • Since 2024 the filter has narrowed to essential services. Punctual Pros, Frontline and CET are all non-discretionary (BSP acquisition methodology).
  • Fair Harbor is the only discretionary consumer bet. It and Frontline are the only portfolio companies with no add-ons (BSP acquisition methodology).

Two kinds of seller

Seller typeAnchor dealsDate
Sponsor secondaryThomas Scientific (Carlyle)Jan 27, 2022
Bully Pulpit International (Svoboda)Apr 27, 2023
Frontline (BV)Dec 11, 2024
Founder or partner, first institutional capitalFair HarborMar 23, 2022
Smith + HowardNov 15, 2022
Punctual ProsApr 3, 2024
CETFeb 2025

(BSP acquisition methodology; BSP firm profile)

  • In secondaries the outgoing sponsor often rolls a minority stake (Svoboda at BPI, BV at Frontline).
  • Inherited CEOs are replaced at about 13-15 months: Simmons to Haas at Thomas, Naidoo to Britt at Frontline.
  • Founder CEOs stay, including Sean Taylor, Matt Buckwalter and John Duquette Jr. (BSP acquisition methodology).

Banked, repeat advisers

  • Six of seven anchor deals had a named sell-side adviser. Punctual Pros went to "eight finalists."
  • Berenson advised BSP on Thomas, BPI, Frontline and CET. Harris Williams advised on Punctual Pros and Frontline.
  • Morrison Cohen or Greenberg Traurig was counsel on every deal (BSP acquisition methodology).

Capital and structure

  • Fund I is about $335M (Form D). The $50-250M check range is unverified (BSP firm profile).
  • Rivals run $0.9-2.1B flagships, so BSP leans on co-invest and operating credibility (est., Private-equity landscape).
  • Financing varies by deal. Thomas used an Apollo/MidCap unitranche maturing in December 2027. Fair Harbor shows equity only on the public record (BSP acquisition methodology).
  • Structures adapt to the sector. At Smith + Howard, BSP invested in the advisory LLC while the CPA firm kept attest work (BSP acquisition methodology).

Add-ons follow the anchor

  • BSP states 23 add-ons. Only 21 are identified by name (BSP acquisition methodology).
  • The landscape suggests BSP should avoid auctions for Punctual Pros add-ons. It recommends proprietary outreach to shops under $3M EBITDA (est., Private-equity landscape).
  • Time to first add-on and add-on multiples are not in this context. Deal-level close dates and pricing would answer both.

Next actions

  • Identify the two unnamed add-ons from Punctual Pros and Smith + Howard records to reconcile the count of 23.
  • Confirm the Fund I size and check range against BSP's internal fund documents.
  • Track Frontline CEO transition outcomes against the 13-15 month replacement pattern.
  • Build a proprietary sub-$3M EBITDA target list for Punctual Pros in Central PA and NJ.

- Founder CEOs stay, including Sean Taylor, Matt Buckwalter and John Duquette Jr. (BSP acquisition methodology).

- Rivals run $0.9-2.1B flagships, so BSP leans on co-invest and operating credibility (est., Private-equity landscape).

- The landscape suggests BSP should avoid auctions for Punctual Pros add-ons. It recommends proprietary outreach to shops under $3M EBITDA (est., Private-equity landscape).
